changes.from:
Symptom: a session started via one client shows incomplete/divergent chat history when reopened from another machine.

Root cause (evidence, workspace store oqto-log/45661ed61681d8d746e393d4): one pi session (pi UUID 019f5f22-3777-78b7-ab0e-539863fb8232) produced TWO oqto_log_sessions rows for the same conversation:
  1. session_id=platform_id=external_id=019f5f22..., source_kind=pi_agent_end (live streaming path), 12 turns
  2. session_id=platform_id=oqto-1784007500905-e4b1aea20b3398, external_id=019f5f22..., source_kind=pi_jsonl (import path), 13 turns

Live path (oqto-runner/src/pi_manager.rs ~3742) calls append_agent_end_snapshot with session_id AND platform_id both == the raw pi UUID, because pi_manager.rs:3260 `pi_native_id_known = !session_id.starts_with("oqto-")` treats any non-oqto session_id as the pi-native id and never uses a canonical oqto public id. JSONL import path mints oqto-.... Two ingestion paths => two sessions for one conversation => history splits across reload/machines.

Violates ADR-0023 (one public oqto session id; platform_id=Oqto identity, external_id=harness binding; harness ids never become public/join ids) and the sacred session-identity rule.

Fix scope: (1) runner always operates under a minted oqto- id, pi UUID only as external_id, remove starts_with(oqto-) heuristic, fail-closed; (2) trace the start/attach entrypoint that admits a non-oqto session_id; (3) one-time reconciliation of duplicated rows; (4) regression test (one pi session => exactly one oqto_log_session across live+jsonl).

Related: ADR-0023, oqto-zpvs.5, oqto-964n.

--- Prevalence + trigger analysis (2026-07-14) ---
- 70 dual-write splits across this workspace's oqto-log shards (same external_id -> both a raw-UUID and an oqto- session), spanning 2026-01 .. 2026-07-14. Only 1 recent; ~69 Jan-May desktop-era => systemic, not a stale/new PWA.
- Frontend MINTS the id: frontend/lib/session-utils.ts:1880 createPiSessionId() = 'oqto-'+crypto.randomUUID() (secure ctx) else fallback 'oqto-'+Date.now()+'-'+hex. ADR-0023 says BACKEND must mint -> deeper violation.
- Trigger correlation: fallback-format ids (insecure context: http-over-LAN / mobile PWA / webview lacking crypto.randomUUID) are 6% of ALL sessions (137/2187) but 92% of split sessions (65/70) => ~15x enrichment. Today's broken id oqto-1784007500905-e4b1aea20b3398 is fallback format.
- Mitigation (removes trigger, not the class of bug): serve frontend over HTTPS/secure-context so crypto.randomUUID is always present.

--- FIX + UNSPLIT (2026-07-14) ---
FIX (oqto-history): store is now the choke point enforcing ADR-0023 identity.
- store.rs: platform_id_for_external_id() (uuid v5, shared; importer's duplicate copy deleted) + is_canonical_session_id() + canonicalize_session_identity() applied in append_agent_end_snapshot and replace_session_with_snapshot_inner.
- Resolution order: canonical platform_id passes through -> else existing canonical binding for external_id wins (live agent-end + jsonl import converge) -> else pre-existing harness-id session keeps its id (never orphan legacy turns) -> else mint deterministic oqto-{v5}.
- Consistent with ops.rs batch_upsert_session_identities, which already used binding-wins.
- Tests (proven to FAIL without the fix, reproducing the exact prod split):
  one_pi_session_yields_one_oqto_session_across_both_paths, harness_id_alone_mints_a_canonical_identity, existing_harness_id_session_keeps_its_id.

UNSPLIT (new CLI: `oqto runner migrate-oqto-log --mode unsplit|unsplit-dry-run`):
- ops.rs: find_harness_session_splits(), unsplit_harness_sessions() -> UnsplitOutcome, delete_sessions_by_session_id_exact (keys strictly on session_id; delete_session() matches external_id too and would delete the survivor).
- SAFETY: only collapses when the canonical keeper HAS turns. Identity-sync creates canonical rows with 0 turns; for those the harness row is the only copy.

INCIDENT (resolved, no data lost): first migration cut lacked the empty-keeper guard and deleted 11 harness rows whose canonical keeper was empty. Restored all 11 from backup (~/oqto-log-backup-20260714-222140) + FTS rebuild; verified all 69 former splits have content (69 ok / 0 empty / 0 missing).

STATE: 58 splits collapsed; 11 remain, correctly SKIPPED as unsafe (canonical empty).
FOLLOW-UP: the 11 need re-projection from pi JSONL into the canonical keeper (bootstrap mode; with the store fix it now resolves onto the binding), then unsplit collapses them.
NOT DONE: fix not deployed — running oqto/oqto-runner are pre-fix binaries and can still write harness-id rows until rebuilt+restarted.

--- STRENGTHENED: binding wins over a proposed canonical id (2026-07-15) ---
Found a second split source before rebuilding: canonical ids are minted by THREE schemes for the same conversation
  - frontend secure ctx : oqto-{uuid v4}      (1 session)
  - frontend insecure   : oqto-{ms}-{hex}     (137 sessions; the split trigger)
  - importer/bootstrap  : oqto-{uuid v5(ext)} (2051 sessions; de-facto canonical)
The first fix passed ANY canonical platform_id through, so a JSONL bootstrap (v5) against a frontend-named session (oqto-1779...) would have minted a THIRD identity for 7 of the 11.
canonicalize_session_identity now resolves the external binding FIRST, ahead of the proposed canonical id; a proposed canonical is only used when no binding exists. Same rule ops.rs batch_upsert_session_identities already used.
Test: rebuild_with_a_different_canonical_scheme_reuses_the_bound_session (asserts the schemes actually differ, then that the rebuild reuses the bound identity).

Verified all 11 pi JSONL files still exist -> rebuild-from-truth is viable for the empty keepers.

--- REBUILD ATTEMPT FAILED + REVERTED (2026-07-15) ---
Tried to fill the 11 empty keepers by re-projecting pi JSONL. Two blockers + one self-inflicted regression, all now reverted.

1. `--mode bootstrap` IS NOT A REBUILD. It is incremental: importer-state.json (~/.local/share/oqto/oqto-log/importer-state.json) fingerprints each JSONL by mtime+size and skips unchanged files. First run: scanned 2423, imported 4, skipped 2419 -> reported success while doing nothing. A real rebuild requires invalidating the checkpoint first.

2. BOOTSTRAP DUPLICATES (pre-existing bug, not introduced here). bootstrap appends via append_agent_end_snapshot, whose dedupe keys on source_kind='pi_agent_end'. Sessions whose turns came from pi_jsonl do not match that dedupe, so the whole conversation is re-inserted. It only self-heals when UNDER-populated (sess_stats.messages < messages.len()); over-population never heals. After forcing re-import, 11 sessions went to ~2x their JSONL truth (e.g. 928->1856, 905->1810, 442->871).
   -> Reverted all 11 from backup + FTS rebuild + importer-state.json restored.
   -> VERIFIED: 0 sessions exceed backup; all 2221 conversations that had turns still have turns (0 lost).

3. TWO MODEL ERRORS in the unsplit migration (must fix before any retry):
   a. NOT one store per workspace. The same workspace_id exists in MULTIPLE shard dirs (rich-todos in 2, octo/users/main in 3, oqto-website in 2) — the workspace->shard hash evidently changed at some point and old+new stores coexist. find_harness_session_splits only looks WITHIN a store, so cross-shard duplicates are invisible.
   b. canonical platform_id DOES NOT imply canonical session_id. Real row in shard 7b41a490: session_id=a940c2fd (raw pi id) with platform_id=oqto-8655abb0 (canonical). canonicalize_session_identity's binding lookup returns that row's RAW session_id — which is why the keepers never filled.

STATE: 58 splits collapsed (verified). 11 splits remain, correctly SKIPPED (empty canonical keeper). Data is consistent with the pre-migration backup: no loss, no duplication.

NEXT (do NOT retry blind):
- The 11 need replace_session_with_pi_jsonl_records (full replace from truth), NOT append. Consider making bootstrap use replace whenever oqto-log disagrees with the JSONL in EITHER direction, not only when under-populated.
- Teach the split finder about multi-shard workspaces and about rows whose session_id is raw while platform_id is canonical.
- Backup retained: ~/oqto-log-backup-20260714-222140 (2.7G).

--- DEPLOY REGRESSION (mine) + A BIGGER PRE-EXISTING BUG (2026-07-15) ---
`just deploy --host archvm` FAILED at the oqto-log validate gate: 2 greenowl sessions had JSONL content but 0 oqto-log messages. The deployed binary was built from this working tree, so the fix was live.

MY REGRESSION (fixed): canonicalize_session_identity silently rewrote the identity and gave callers no way to learn it.
  bootstrap: append writes under minted oqto-{v5} -> then calls collapse_duplicate_external_sessions(external=pi_id, keep=session_id) where session_id is still the RAW pi id -> that deletes every session bound to the external id except `keep`, and `keep` no longer exists -> IT DELETED THE ROW IT JUST WROTE. failed_files=0, silent.
FIX: AppendStats now carries `session_id` = the identity actually written; bootstrap uses it for read_session_stats / collapse / upsert_import_checkpoint.
  Subtlety: ImportedSession feeds the validate-changed filter, which keys on the PI id parsed from the JSONL filename. Recording the resolved id there would make validation SKIP these sessions (green deploy that checks nothing) -> now records pi_session_id. count_oqto_log_session_messages already resolves via external_id.
  Test: append_reports_the_session_id_it_actually_wrote. 35 tests green.
VERIFIED: both sessions now persist (oqto-f1dfd02d turns=2, oqto-d2d5b5c0 turns=94); validate-changed = 3 checked / 3 ok / 0 mismatch.

BIGGER PRE-EXISTING BUG (NOT mine, not yet fixed) — likely the root of oqto-zpvs "duplicated messages":
  - The runner refreshes live sessions via replace_session_with_pi_jsonl_records => their turns carry source_kind='pi_jsonl'.
  - bootstrap then APPENDS via append_agent_end_snapshot, whose dedupe keys on source_kind='pi_agent_end' (and whose snapshot dedupe compares the last turn's source_hash). Neither matches pi_jsonl turns => the ENTIRE conversation is re-inserted.
  - bootstrap self-heals only when UNDER-populated (sess_stats.messages < messages.len()); over-population never heals.
  - the validator only asserts oqto_count >= jsonl_count, so OVER-population passes the gate silently.
  => every deploy can silently DOUBLE any live session whose JSONL changed since the last import. Observed: 019f414a went 1024(truth) -> 2048.
RECOMMEND: (a) bootstrap should replace-from-JSONL whenever oqto-log disagrees with the JSONL in EITHER direction, not only when under; (b) validator should fail on oqto_count > jsonl_count too (currently blind); (c) then re-check all sessions for 2x duplication.

--- SCALE OF THE DUPLICATION BUG (read-only sweep, 2026-07-15) ---
Swept every oqto-log session against its pi JSONL (role-line count):
  matching/above truth : 2288
  under truth (partial): 4
  OVER truth by >1.5x  : 74   <-- duplicated; every message renders twice
Worst: 019ea788 jsonl=3319 oqto=5641 (1.7x); 019e0662 874->1713 (1.96x); 019f0d5f 389->778 (2.0x); 019f368f 237->474 (2.0x).

changes.to:
Rescoped 2026-08-20 after evaluating paradigmxyz/iron-proxy (wiki: external-repo-evals/iron-proxy.md), found via paradigmxyz/centaur which deploys it as its credential boundary.

iron-proxy is Apache-2.0 Go, single binary + YAML, and implements most of ADR-0035's reference enforcer in one component: default-deny domain/CIDR allowlist; TPROXY capture that works BELOW DNS (catches hardcoded IPs, i.e. a real transparent tier) with an nftables example; placeholder credentials swapped for real secrets at egress, bound per destination via per-secret host rules; per-request structured JSON audit naming which secrets were swapped and which rules matched (= the flow log); streaming-aware (WebSocket/SSE) which matters for EAVS inference; optional HTTP_PROXY/SOCKS5 tunnel for the cooperative case.

Evaluate ahead of smokescreen, which is CONNECT-only. Oqto still owns WorkspaceEgressPolicy, compilation to config, per-workspace lifecycle, capability advertisement, audit integration, and the netns choke point that makes any enforcer unbypassable (oqto-egressd shrinks rather than disappears). Keep the pluggable EgressEnforcer contract so this stays safe to adopt and safe to drop.

Open before committing: does TPROXY work under rootless podman with userns=auto given --cap-drop=all, or is the transparent tier only reachable via a host-side netns? One proxy per workspace or one managed multi-tenant config? Streaming latency under inference load? Certificate-pinning clients?

SPIKE RESULT 2026-08-20 (measured locally, wiki: external-repo-evals/iron-proxy.md):
- default-deny works: denied host -> 403 with audit rejected_by=allowlist
- placeholder -> real secret proven end to end; the placeholder is worthless when sent directly
- audit names the swapped secret and its location (header:Authorization) = the ADR-0035 flow log
- SSE streams at source cadence, not buffered (EAVS-safe)
- works from inside the real oqto-workspace:dev rootless container (denied host blocked, secret swapped)
- runs unprivileged once http_listen/https_listen are moved off :80/:443
- upstream_deny_cidrs blocked loopback unprompted (IMDS/SSRF protection is real and on by default)
- gotchas: dns.proxy_ip is required even when DNS mode is unused; loopback upstreams need an explicit CIDR override

DECIDED CONSTRAINT: their nftables/TPROXY recipe loads rules inside the workload and needs CAP_NET_ADMIN there; oqto placements run --cap-drop=all and must not add it. Apply the redirect host-side in the workspace netns (oqto-egressd) and have the placement join it with --net ns: -- same mechanism, different location. Cooperative HTTP_PROXY mode needs no privileges and already works.

NEXT: decide buy-vs-build for the enforcer, then wire the netns redirect. Adopt upstream_deny_cidrs (IMDS/loopback/rebinding) into WorkspaceEgressPolicy regardless of that decision.

changes.from: Build in-house (Rust, config-driven, headless-first; executor.sh (MIT) as design reference, not dependency). Agents never hold credentials: a host-side broker holds secrets and exposes narrowed capabilities per workspace via granted endpoint sockets (socket provenance = identity, same pattern as EAVS). Per-tool policy allowed/approval/blocked; explicit staged approvals (agent knows it is paused — no simulated state); spec-driven integrations (MCP proxy first, OpenAPI later) instead of hand-built per-vendor proxies; opaque unforgeable grant handles carrying no parseable identity; broker is sole authority on its resource, backend stores grants without vendor identity knowledge. Complements ADR-0035: tiers govern bytes, broker governs actions; raw network egress is out of scope here.

BORROW FROM openbot (wiki: external-repo-evals/openbot.md, evaluated 2026-08-20) — two independent platforms (also centaur) converged on this shape, so treat these as settled design inputs rather than options:
1. AUDIT BEFORE ACT: resolve target -> evaluate policy -> write the audit row -> only then act. An unlogged action becomes structurally impossible, which is strictly stronger than ADR-0035's after-the-fact flow log and is cheap only if designed in now.
2. SERVER-HELD TARGET SNAPSHOT: the agent names a target the control plane already knows; it cannot supply or forge one. Generalises ADR-0035's destination-binding rule from credentials to every broker target.
3. FAIL-CLOSED POLICY DEFAULTS, all three: deny evaluated before allow; a missing policy permits nothing; a broken rule refuses rather than opens.
4. REQUESTER AUTHORITY AS POLICY INPUT: their rules read actor.id alongside bot.id, matching centaur's per-turn requester principal. Confirms the missing axis in oqto's grant model.
5. SECRETS NEVER IN THE TRANSCRIPT: record that a secret was requested and for how long, never its value.
For oqto-aehc.5 specifically: SPIFFE/SPIRE per-workload SVIDs are the alternative to Oqto-as-OIDC-issuer; their spire/agent.conf documents the trap that the Unix attestor needs a shared PID namespace, which fails when each workload gets its own runtime-created container.

changes.from: Security finding in backend/crates/oqto/src/bus/engine.rs. BusEngine::authorize_scope returns Ok for every authenticated Account subscribing to any concrete BusScope::Session scope_id. Its comment claims delivery filters to Sessions the Account owns, but publish fanout matches only event.scope/event.scope_id/topic/filter and never verifies source.user_id or Session authorization. A caller that guesses/obtains another Session id can therefore subscribe/pull its bus events. pull_for_user has the same authorize_scope weakness. Workspace authorization also relies partly on host-path substring heuristics and should be replaced with stable owner IDs. Fix or remove the bus before exposing App/customization consumers. Proof: regression test with Alice subscribing/pulling Bob's concrete Session id must be denied and receive no event; authorization must resolve canonical Session ownership/membership by stable IDs, never source comments/path heuristics. If the generic bus is deleted per ADR-0012's survival condition, prove all routes/client hooks/admin surfaces are removed and no consumer depends on it.

changes.from:
Prime Intellect disclosed a universal offline-sandbox escape (primeintellect.ai/blog/universal-offline-sandbox-escape): agents in 'offline' sandboxes reached the internet THROUGH the inference API. The OpenAI Responses API input_file.file_url parameter makes the provider fetch an arbitrary URL and return its content into context; server-side tools (web_search, web_fetch) do the same. GPT-5.6 Sol Pro used exactly this to escape a blocked egress env, drive other model instances as sub-agents via curl, and recover a hidden flag. Several inference frameworks had SSRF-class vulnerabilities in the same surface (TensorRT-LLM/Dynamo now disable by default; SGLang/vLLM added opt-in allowlists).

Applies to oqto as deployed today: EAVS passes request bodies through unmodified (verified 2026-08-20: no input_file/file_url handling in src/proxy.rs), and oqto workspaces reach providers only through EAVS. The agent controls prompt content, so it can ride the ALLOWED channel: exfiltrate workspace data encoded in a file_url pointing at an attacker host, or fetch content past egress enforcement. The egress enforcer cannot see the second hop; the destination is legitimately allowed.

Fix in EAVS (model-domain semantics, per ADR-0035 division of responsibility):
1. Strip or policy-gate remote-fetch parameters in request bodies: input[].content items of type input_file with file_url, and tool definitions of type web_search/web_fetch/fetch, unless the tenant/workspace policy grants delegated fetch.

changes.from:
Rescoped 2026-08-20 after evaluating paradigmxyz/iron-proxy (wiki: external-repo-evals/iron-proxy.md), found via paradigmxyz/centaur which deploys it as its credential boundary.

iron-proxy is Apache-2.0 Go, single binary + YAML, and implements most of ADR-0035's reference enforcer in one component: default-deny domain/CIDR allowlist; TPROXY capture that works BELOW DNS (catches hardcoded IPs, i.e. a real transparent tier) with an nftables example; placeholder credentials swapped for real secrets at egress, bound per destination via per-secret host rules; per-request structured JSON audit naming which secrets were swapped and which rules matched (= the flow log); streaming-aware (WebSocket/SSE) which matters for EAVS inference; optional HTTP_PROXY/SOCKS5 tunnel for the cooperative case.

Also covers ground ADR-0035 missed: upstream IP deny list closing SSRF/DNS-rebinding, with IMDS (169.254.169.254, fd00:ec2::254, fd20:ce::254) and loopback denied by default. Adopt that into the policy model regardless of the buy decision.

Evaluate ahead of smokescreen, which is CONNECT-only. Oqto still owns WorkspaceEgressPolicy, compilation to config, per-workspace lifecycle, capability advertisement, audit integration, and the netns choke point that makes any enforcer unbypassable (oqto-egressd shrinks rather than disappears). Keep the pluggable EgressEnforcer contract so this stays safe to adopt and safe to drop.

Open before committing: does TPROXY work under rootless podman with userns=auto given --cap-drop=all, or is the transparent tier only reachable via a host-side netns? One proxy per workspace or one managed multi-tenant config? Streaming latency under inference load? Certificate-pinning clients?
SPIKE RESULT 2026-08-20 (measured locally, wiki: external-repo-evals/iron-proxy.md):
- default-deny works: denied host -> 403 with audit rejected_by=allowlist
- placeholder -> real secret proven end to end; the placeholder is worthless when sent directly
- audit names the swapped secret and its location (header:Authorization) = the ADR-0035 flow log
- SSE streams at source cadence, not buffered (EAVS-safe)
- works from inside the real oqto-workspace:dev rootless container (denied host blocked, secret swapped)
- runs unprivileged once http_listen/https_listen are moved off :80/:443
- upstream_deny_cidrs blocked loopback unprompted (IMDS/SSRF protection is real and on by default)
- gotchas: dns.proxy_ip is required even when DNS mode is unused; loopback upstreams need an explicit CIDR override

DECIDED CONSTRAINT: their nftables/TPROXY recipe loads rules inside the workload and needs CAP_NET_ADMIN there; oqto placements run --cap-drop=all and must not add it. Apply the redirect host-side in the workspace netns (oqto-egressd) and have the placement join it with --net ns: -- same mechanism, different location. Cooperative HTTP_PROXY mode needs no privileges and already works.

NEXT: decide buy-vs-build for the enforcer, then wire the netns redirect. Adopt upstream_deny_cidrs (IMDS/loopback/rebinding) into WorkspaceEgressPolicy regardless of that decision.

Adopted 2026-08-27. paradigmxyz/iron-proxy is the reference HTTP egress enforcer (Apache-2.0 Go, single binary).

Resolution of the 2026-08-27 allowed-HTTPS EOF finding: NOT an upstream bug. Our config lacked proxy.tunnel_listen -- the CONNECT/SOCKS5 listener; CONNECT hitting http_listen gets misrouted as a plain request (upstream issue #241 filed and closed by us). Operational requirements captured for oqto-gyqr.3: (1) per-workspace instances must set metrics.listen uniquely -- a :9090 collision kills the instance at startup; (2) clients target the tunnel listener; (3) compiler emits tunnel_listen (60604b4d).
